title: Avtale og bekrefte en time — arrange and confirm an appointment
goal: Ask about availability, accept or reject a slot, make a counterproposal, and confirm the purpose, date, and time.

objectives.statement: Ask about availability, accept or reject a slot, make a counterproposal, and confirm the purpose, date, and time.

spans.value: Mina uses her bicycle every day. Recently, the brakes have started making a strange noise, so she calls a local workshop.
Sykkelverkstedet, det er Erik.
Hei. Jeg vil gjerne bestille en time for å sjekke bremsene.

blocks.translation: Hello. I’d like to make an appointment to have the brakes checked.

spans.value: Ja, selvfølgelig. Når passer det for deg?

blocks.translation: Yes, of course. When works for you?

spans.value: Har dere noe ledig torsdag ettermiddag?

blocks.translation: Do you have anything available on Thursday afternoon?

spans.value: Vi har en ledig time klokka halv tre.

blocks.translation: We have an available appointment at half past two.

spans.value: Dessverre passer ikke det. Jeg er på jobb til klokka fire. Kan jeg komme etter klokka fire?

blocks.translation: Unfortunately, that doesn’t suit me. I’m at work until four. Can I come after four?

spans.value: Ikke på torsdag, men hva med fredag klokka kvart over fire?

blocks.translation: Not on Thursday, but how about Friday at quarter past four?

spans.value: Ja, det passer fint.
Flott. Da setter jeg deg opp fredag 14. mars klokka 16.15 for en bremsesjekk. Stemmer det?

blocks.translation: Great. Then I’ll book you in for Friday, 14 March, at 4:15 p.m. for a brake check. Is that correct?

spans.value: Ja, det stemmer. Fredag 14. mars klokka kvart over fire.

blocks.translation: Yes, that’s correct. Friday, 14 March, at quarter past four.

spans.value: Fint. Da sees vi på fredag.

blocks.translation: Good. See you on Friday, then.

spans.value: Takk. Ha det!

Mina does not simply ask for an appointment and accept the first suggestion. She asks what is available, rejects a time that conflicts with work, proposes a different part of the day, and accepts a new slot. Erik then checks the purpose, date, and time; Mina confirms his summary and explicitly repeats the date and time. This sequence is useful for appointments with workshops, doctors, dentists, hairdressers, public offices, and many other services.
A common way to begin is:

no.value: Jeg vil gjerne bestille en time.

en.value: I’d like to make an appointment.

spans.value: Here,
en time
means an appointment or booked session. In other contexts, it can also mean an hour. The situation normally makes the meaning clear.
You can add the purpose with
for

no.value: Jeg vil gjerne bestille en time for en synstest.

en.value: I’d like to make an appointment for an eye test.

no.value: Jeg vil gjerne bestille en time for en hårklipp.

en.value: I’d like to make an appointment for a haircut.

spans.value: You can also use
for å
followed by an action:

no.value: Jeg vil gjerne bestille en time for å sjekke bremsene.

en.value: I’d like to make an appointment to have the brakes checked.

no.value: Jeg vil gjerne bestille en time for å snakke med legen.

en.value: I’d like to make an appointment to speak with the doctor.

spans.value: In Mina’s call, the purpose is clear from the beginning: the bicycle brakes need checking. This allows Erik to confirm not only when she is coming, but also what the workshop should do.
Mina has trouble reading distant text and calls an optician. Choose the appointment purpose that fits her need.
Once the purpose is clear, you need to find a possible time. Mina asks:

no.value: Har dere noe ledig torsdag ettermiddag?

en.value: Do you have anything available on Thursday afternoon?

spans.value: Ledig
means available or free. You can ask broadly:

no.value: Har dere noe ledig neste uke?

en.value: Do you have anything available next week?

no.value: Har du noe ledig på mandag?

en.value: Do you have anything available on Monday?

spans.value: Use
dere
when asking about the business’s or staff’s availability. Use
du
when asking the individual interlocutor what works for them, including an employee who answers on behalf of a business.
You can also ask about a specific time:

no.value: Er klokka ti ledig?

en.value: Is ten o’clock available?

no.value: Har dere en ledig time klokka tre?

en.value: Do you have an available appointment at three?

spans.value: Another useful question is:

no.value: Når har dere en ledig time?

en.value: When do you have an available appointment?

spans.value: Compare the questions:

no.value: Har dere noe ledig på tirsdag?

en.value: Do you have anything available on Tuesday?

spans.value: This asks whether Tuesday has any possible slots.

no.value: Når har dere noe ledig?

en.value: When do you have anything available?

spans.value: This leaves the day and time open.

no.value: Passer tirsdag for deg?

en.value: Does Tuesday suit you?

spans.value: This asks whether Tuesday works for the other person, not whether a business has an open slot.
Time expressions often move naturally to the end:

no.value: Har dere noe ledig fredag morgen?

en.value: Do you have anything available on Friday morning?

no.value: Har dere noe ledig etter lunsj?

en.value: Do you have anything available after lunch?

no.value: Har dere noe ledig mellom klokka to og fire?

en.value: Do you have anything available between two and four?

spans.value: The optician's calendar is full on Monday and Tuesday morning, but Tuesday afternoon is open. Choose the question that asks the business about that open period.
Erik replies:

no.value: Vi har en ledig time klokka halv tre.

en.value: We have an available appointment at half past two.

spans.value: Norwegian clock expressions need careful attention.
Halv tre
means halfway to three, so it is 2:30, not 3:30.

no.value: halv ni

en.value: half past eight

no.value: kvart over fire

en.value: quarter past four

no.value: kvart på fem

en.value: quarter to five

spans.value: Appointments may also be stated with the twenty-four-hour clock:

no.value: Timen er klokka 14.30.

en.value: The appointment is at 2:30 p.m.

no.value: Vi kan tilby en time klokka 16.15.

en.value: We can offer an appointment at 4:15 p.m.

spans.value: In everyday conversation, Mina repeats
as
kvart over fire
. Both refer to the same time.
An offered slot often appears in one of these patterns:

no.value: Vi har en ledig time på onsdag klokka elleve.

en.value: We have an available appointment on Wednesday at eleven.

no.value: Du kan komme torsdag morgen.

en.value: You can come on Thursday morning.

no.value: Hva med fredag klokka kvart over fire?

en.value: How about Friday at quarter past four?

no.value: Passer mandag klokka ni?

en.value: Does Monday at nine suit you?

spans.value: The last two forms invite you to accept, reject, or make another suggestion.
Mina accepts the Friday appointment with:

no.value: Ja, det passer fint.

en.value: Yes, that suits me well.

spans.value: Other natural confirmations include:

no.value: Ja, det passer bra.

en.value: Yes, that works well.

no.value: Det passer perfekt.

en.value: That works perfectly.

no.value: Fredag klokka fire passer for meg.

en.value: Friday at four works for me.

spans.value: A short
Ja, det passer
is often enough when the proposed time is already clear.
Compare:

no.value: Ja, fredag passer fint.

en.value: Yes, Friday suits me well.

spans.value: This confirms the day, but not necessarily a particular time.

no.value: Ja, fredag klokka fire passer fint.

en.value: Yes, Friday at four suits me well.

spans.value: This confirms both day and time and is safer when several slots have been discussed.
The receptionist offers Wednesday at ten, after Mina finishes work at nine. Choose the response that accepts the exact offered slot so both speakers confirm the same time.
The first appointment does not work for Mina:

no.value: Dessverre passer ikke det.

en.value: Unfortunately, that doesn’t suit me.

spans.value: This is direct but polite. You can add a short reason:

no.value: Dessverre passer ikke det. Jeg er på jobb da.

en.value: Unfortunately, that doesn’t suit me. I’m at work then.

no.value: Tirsdag passer ikke for meg. Jeg er bortreist.

en.value: Tuesday doesn’t work for me. I’m away.

no.value: Jeg kan dessverre ikke komme klokka ti.

en.value: Unfortunately, I can’t come at ten.

spans.value: Notice where
ikke
appears:

no.value: Det passer ikke.

en.value: That doesn’t suit me.

no.value: Jeg kan ikke komme.

en.value: I can’t come.

spans.value: A common mistake is to reject the time without showing what should happen next:

no.value: Nei, det passer ikke.

en.value: No, that doesn’t suit me.

spans.value: This is understandable, but the conversation may stop unless the other person makes another offer. Mina keeps the arrangement moving by adding a limit:

no.value: Jeg er på jobb til klokka fire. Kan jeg komme etter klokka fire?

en.value: I’m at work until four. Can I come after four?

spans.value: A counterproposal is a new suggestion after the first slot does not work. Mina asks:

no.value: Kan jeg komme etter klokka fire?

en.value: Can I come after four?

spans.value: You can suggest a specific alternative:

no.value: Kan jeg komme klokka halv fem i stedet?

en.value: Can I come at half past four instead?

no.value: Passer fredag klokka ti?

en.value: Does Friday at ten suit you?

no.value: Hva med torsdag ettermiddag?

en.value: How about Thursday afternoon?

no.value: Har dere noe ledig litt senere?

en.value: Do you have anything available a little later?

spans.value: You can also state when you are free:

no.value: Jeg kan på mandag etter klokka to.

en.value: I’m available on Monday after two.

no.value: Jeg kan ikke om morgenen, men jeg kan om ettermiddagen.

en.value: I can’t in the morning, but I can in the afternoon.

no.value: Onsdag er vanskelig, men torsdag passer bra.

en.value: Wednesday is difficult, but Thursday works well.

spans.value: A useful appointment exchange often follows this pattern:

no.value: Passer tirsdag klokka ett?

en.value: Does Tuesday at one suit you?

no.value: Dessverre passer ikke det. Hva med onsdag morgen?

en.value: Unfortunately, that doesn’t suit me. How about Wednesday morning?

spans.value: The rejection and new suggestion belong together. The first sentence closes one possibility; the second opens another.

no.value: Det passer ikke.

en.value: That doesn’t work.

spans.value: This rejects the suggestion but gives no alternative.

no.value: Det passer ikke, men jeg kan etter klokka tre.

en.value: That doesn’t work, but I’m available after three.

spans.value: This rejects the suggestion and gives a useful time range.

no.value: Kan jeg komme senere?

en.value: Can I come later?

spans.value: This asks for a change but remains broad.

no.value: Kan jeg komme klokka halv fem i stedet?

en.value: Can I come at half past four instead?

spans.value: This gives a precise counterproposal.

The workshop offers Tuesday at one. Mina's calendar shows that she works from nine to four on Tuesday and is free Wednesday morning. Choose the response that rejects the conflict and proposes a possible alternative.
After Mina accepts the Friday slot, Erik confirms all essential details:

no.value: Da setter jeg deg opp fredag 14. mars klokka 16.15 for en bremsesjekk. Stemmer det?

en.value: Then I’ll book you in for Friday, 14 March, at 4:15 p.m. for a brake check. Is that correct?

spans.value: Å sette noen opp
means to enter someone in a schedule or book them in.

no.value: Jeg setter deg opp på mandag klokka ni.

en.value: I’ll book you in for Monday at nine.

spans.value: For learners, the most important part is recognizing and checking the complete appointment:
Mina confirms Erik’s summary and explicitly repeats the date and time:

no.value: Ja, det stemmer. Fredag 14. mars klokka kvart over fire.

en.value: Yes, that’s correct. Friday, 14 March, at quarter past four.

spans.value: Useful checking questions include:

no.value: Stemmer det?

en.value: Is that correct?

no.value: Var det fredag klokka fire?

en.value: Was it Friday at four?

no.value: Bare for å bekrefte: Timen er torsdag 8. mai klokka 10.30?

en.value: Just to confirm: The appointment is Thursday, 8 May, at 10:30?

no.value: Og timen gjelder en synstest, ikke sant?

en.value: And the appointment is for an eye test, right?

spans.value: If a detail is wrong, correct that detail clearly:

no.value: Nei, det er fredag, ikke torsdag.

en.value: No, it’s Friday, not Thursday.

no.value: Timen er klokka halv to, ikke halv tre.

en.value: The appointment is at half past one, not half past two.

no.value: Jeg bestilte time for en hårklipp, ikke for farging.

en.value: I booked an appointment for a haircut, not for coloring.

spans.value: Repeating the complete appointment is especially useful when several dates or times have appeared in the conversation.
Mina's appointment card shows a bicycle brake check on Friday 14 March at 16:15. Choose the confirmation that preserves the service, date, and time.
Confusing an appointment with availability

no.value: Jeg har en time fredag.

en.value: I have an appointment on Friday.

spans.value: This reports an existing appointment.

no.value: Har dere en time fredag?

en.value: Do you have an appointment on Friday?

spans.value: This may be understood, but it can sound as though you are asking whether the business itself has an appointment. For availability, this is clearer:

no.value: Har dere en ledig time fredag?

en.value: Do you have an available appointment on Friday?

spans.value: Confusing Norwegian half-hours
Klokka halv tre
means 2:30.
Klokka halv fire
means 3:30.
If you are unsure, confirm with the twenty-four-hour time:

no.value: Mener du klokka 14.30?

en.value: Do you mean 2:30 p.m.?

spans.value: Accepting an unclear slot
If two times have been discussed,
Det passer
may be too vague. Repeat the selected slot:

no.value: Fredag klokka 16.15 passer fint.

en.value: Friday at 4:15 p.m. works well.

spans.value: Rejecting without helping the conversation continue

no.value: Nei, jeg kan ikke.

en.value: No, I can’t.

spans.value: This rejects the offer, but gives the other person little guidance.

no.value: Jeg kan dessverre ikke på tirsdag. Har dere noe ledig på onsdag?

en.value: Unfortunately, I can’t on Tuesday. Do you have anything available on Wednesday?

spans.value: This makes the next step clear.
Confirming only one detail

no.value: Ja, fredag stemmer.

en.value: Yes, Friday is correct.

spans.value: The day may be right while the time or purpose is wrong. For a complete confirmation, include the full arrangement:

no.value: Ja, det stemmer: fredag 14. mars klokka 16.15 for en bremsesjekk.

en.value: Yes, that’s correct: Friday, 14 March, at 4:15 p.m. for a brake check.

spans.value: The same booking details may be read back later:
Fredag 14. mars klokka 16.15 for en bremsesjekk.

blocks.translation: Friday, 14 March, at 4:15 p.m. for a brake check.

spans.value: Det stemmer.
This brief example reinforces recognition and confirmation of the same purpose, date, and time from the original call.

Using the request, availability, rejection, counterproposal, acceptance, and confirmation patterns practiced above, create a short appointment exchange based on a practical situation. Begin with a clear purpose, ask what is available, and respond to the first proposed slot. Make that first slot unsuitable so that you must reject it and offer another possibility. Then accept a workable slot and confirm the purpose, date, and time.

Keep the exchange focused on arranging one appointment. Your response should move logically from request to availability, rejection, counterproposal, acceptance, and final confirmation, with both speakers understanding the same booking.

Without looking back, write three short Norwegian customer turns in response to a workshop's supplied offers: ask about availability, reject a conflicting slot while suggesting another, and confirm the accepted brake-check appointment with its date and time.

criteria.instruction: The response is a Norwegian chat exchange between Nora and the salon.
Nora communicates that the appointment is for a haircut.
Nora asks about availability Friday afternoon.
Nora rejects Friday 2 October at 13.00 because she works until 14.00.
Nora asks for or proposes a time after 15.00.
Nora accepts Friday 2 October at 15.30.
The exchange confirms the haircut, Friday 2 October, and 15.30.
The exchange concerns one appointment and does not contradict the supplied facts.
